# Neo theme font tokens name no generic family, so headings turn serif

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

`examples/tableFiltering` shows its title ("Table Filtering") and its intro line in the browser's default serif font, both on the page and on its new example cover. Asked through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode`) on a fresh clone of `dev` (`c722f02bad`), Chrome rendered the `h1` and the `p` with **Times**, while a button on the same page rendered with **Helvetica**.

## The Problem

The neo themes declare their three font-family tokens as single family names with no generic family after them (`resources/css/theme-neo-light/Global.css:9`–`:11`, the same lines in `theme-neo-dark`):

```css
--core-fontfamily-mono : 'Source Code Pro';
--core-fontfamily-sans : 'Source Sans 3';
--core-fontfamily-serif: 'Source Serif Pro';
```

Only the Portal and Legit apps load these fonts, through a Google Fonts link in their `index.html`. On every other page, including every example, the token names a font the page does not have, and with no generic family left in the list the browser falls back to its default font: a serif. A code font from `--core-fontfamily-mono` turns into a proportional serif the same way.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/css/src/Global.css` styles bare `h1`–`h3` and `p` with `font-family: var(--core-fontfamily-sans, revert)` (`:86`, `:98`). The `--sem-typo-*-fontFamily` tokens in both theme files, `app/content/PageContainer.css:51` and `:63` read the same token; `--global-code-font-family` reads `--core-fontfamily-mono`.
- `--neo-font-family` in the same theme files already reads `'Source Sans 3', sans-serif`. `.neo-body` and `examples/grid/headerGroups` use it, which is why they never turn serif.
- Two consumers append the missing fallback themselves: `theme-neo-light/button/Base.css:6` and `theme-neo-dark/button/Base.css:6` (`var(--core-fontfamily-sans), sans-serif`, hence the Helvetica button), and `apps/portal/home/parts/AudienceDoors.css:118` (`var(--core-fontfamily-mono), monospace`).
- Design authority: the contract comment above the element rules in `resources/css/src/Global.css` (#18232): "a family that declares the token gets its value, a family that does not gets the UA stylesheet." The neo family declares the token, yet its pages get the browser's default font whenever Source Sans 3 is missing.

## The Fix

1. In `resources/css/theme-neo-light/Global.css` and `resources/css/theme-neo-dark/Global.css`, end each family token with its generic family: `'Source Code Pro', monospace`, `'Source Sans 3', sans-serif`, `'Source Serif Pro', serif`.
2. Drop the fallbacks the consumers now no longer need: `, sans-serif` in both `button/Base.css` files and `, monospace` in `AudienceDoors.css`.
3. Rebuild the themes (`npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all`) to see the result; `CONTRIBUTING.md` explains why styles need that step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In both neo themes, `--core-fontfamily-mono`, `--core-fontfamily-sans` and `--core-fontfamily-serif` end with `monospace`, `sans-serif` and `serif`.
- [ ] A unit spec reads both theme files and asserts that.
- [ ] `examples/tableFiltering`'s title and intro render in a sans-serif font. The pull request shows the example's first frame at 1440 × 900, before and after.
- [ ] The three consumer-side fallbacks are gone, and the button and the Portal's audience doors still name the same fonts.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes, and so does `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/component/GlobalTypographyNesting.spec.mjs` (it checks the code font).

## Out of Scope

- Loading the Source fonts on example pages: that is a font-loading choice, not a missing fallback.
- The classic themes (`theme-light`, `theme-dark`, `theme-cyberpunk`), which set these tokens to `initial` on purpose so their pages keep the browser's styles.
- Restyling the table-filtering title the way headerGroups styles its own.

## Avoided Traps

- **A class and a stylesheet for tableFiltering's `h1`/`p`** (headerGroups' route): it fixes one example and leaves every other bare heading and paragraph serif.
- **Appending `, sans-serif` in `Global.css`** (`var(--core-fontfamily-sans, revert), sans-serif`): under a classic theme the token is `initial`, the substitution puts `revert` into a list, and that is invalid at computed-value time, so `font-family` falls to `unset` instead of the browser's stylesheet (rule 2 of the comment there).

## Related

#18232 (the `Global.css` typography contract) · #21203 (the table-filtering renewal)
